name: Flupentixol + Melitracen
meta: Flupentixol: Thioxanthene antipsychotic (low dose: anxiolytic–antidepressant); Melitracen: Tricyclic antidepressant
Prescription-only fixed-dose combination. Components – Flupentixol: Schedule H –
prescription only; Melitracen: Schedule H – prescription only
sections: Flupentixol: Developed by Lundbeck from 1963 research into thioxanthenes; the decanoate depot was introduced in 1968. First approval/introduction: Introduced 1965 (H. Lundbeck A/S, Denmark). Melitracen: A tricyclic antidepressant marketed alone and in fixed combination with flupentixol (Lundbeck); the combination is not marketed in its country of origin, Denmark. First approval/introduction: Developed by Kefalas/Lundbeck (1960s); marketed in Europe and Asia.

Low-dose flupentixol has anxiolytic and mood-elevating effects; melitracen is an activating tricyclic antidepressant. The combination provides complementary anxiolytic–antidepressant action with rapid onset.

Flupentixol Dopamine D1/D2 receptor antagonist. At low doses it preferentially blocks presynaptic dopamine autoreceptors, enhancing dopaminergic transmission and producing mood-elevating and anxiolytic effects. Receptor / target profile: D1/D2 antagonist; at low doses it may preferentially act on presynaptic D2 autoreceptors, increasing dopamine release and producing antidepressant effects.

Melitracen Inhibits reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin; low-dose activating antidepressant effect that complements low-dose flupentixol. Receptor / target profile: Monoamine reuptake inhibitor with effects comparable to imipramine and amitriptyline; reportedly faster onset and better tolerability.
Gut wall and hepatic (sulfoxidation, N-dealkylation, glucuronidation)
Summary: Oral bioavailability ~40%; Tmax ~4 h. Metabolised in liver. Half-life ~35 h.
Summary: Well absorbed; Tmax ~4 h. Metabolised in liver. Half-life ~19 h.
Mild-to-moderate depression with anxiety, including psychogenic depression, depressive neuroses and psychosomatic affections with anxiety
Functional dyspepsia / IBS with anxiety–depression (off-label use)
Adults: 2 tablets daily – both in the morning, or one in the morning and one at midday
Severe cases: morning dose may be increased to 2 tablets (max 4 tablets/day)
Not recommended in children and adolescents
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Use lower doses; increased mortality in dementia.
Recent myocardial infarction, heart block, arrhythmias
Extrapyramidal symptoms and tardive dyskinesia (rare at low dose)
Seizure disorders, Parkinson's disease, cardiovascular disease
Anticholinergic effects – caution in prostatic hypertrophy, glaucoma
Flupentixol: Take early in the day; avoid alcohol.
Flupentixol: EPS; ECG in cardiac disease; LFTs on long-term use.
Flupentixol: Somnolence, coma, EPS, convulsions, shock. Supportive care. Melitracen: Anticholinergic toxicity, arrhythmias, seizures, coma. Supportive care, ECG monitoring.
Small randomised studies (largely in Asia) report benefit in mixed anxiety–depression and functional dyspepsia; high-quality large trials are lacking.
Avoid evening doses – may cause insomnia
May cause dry mouth and constipation
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
